title: Systolic blood pressure during the first 72 hours after mechanical thrombectomy and functional outcome — a single-centre retrospective cohort study
summary: After successful mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke, the optimal blood pressure target in the first hours is uncertain. This single-centre, retrospective cohort study uses existing routine and registry data to examine whether the systolic blood pressure achieved within 72 hours after thrombectomy is associated with functional independence at 90 days, as well as with haemorrhagic transformation, symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage and mortality, and explores whether this association depends on the degree of reperfusion.

interventions.name: A single, retrospectively defined cohort of adult patients treated at University Hospital Bonn for acute ischaemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation, who underwent mechanical thrombectomy with successful reperfusion (defined as mTICI 2b–3), is observed. No intervention

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Acute ischaemic stroke with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion (intracranial internal carotid artery, M1 or M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery); mechanical thrombectomy performed; successful recanalisation (mTICI 2b–3); pre-stroke mRS 0–2; ASPECTS ≥ 6.
Exclusion criteria:
Posterior-circulation occlusion or isolated distal location (A2, P2, M3/M4); evidence of haemorrhage on initial imaging; missing documented 90-day mRS.
